target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction & Prerequisite Visuals
lecture_lines: Can we find four points forming a square?
Any simple closed curve allows this configuration.
Visualize a messy loop of string.
Place a square stencil on the loop.
All four corners touch the string.
animations: Fade in simple closed loop in #FFFFFF.
Highlight four points forming a general quadrilateral on the curve in #FFD700.
Morph the quadrilateral to form a perfect square in #FFD700.
Fade out quadrilateral, leave square corners as labels.
Flash all four square corners to emphasize touching the loop.

sections.title: Mapping the Geometry to Topology
lecture_lines: Define a square by center and side length.
Map point relations to square symmetry.
Rotate the square to find zero error.
animations: Show square with center (x, y) and side s in #00FFFF.
Animate rotation of the square, moving vertices along the curve.
Display a continuous graph of placement error reaching zero in #FF4500.

sections.title: The Symmetry Argument
lecture_lines: Inscribed rectangles form a continuous surface.
Identify the diagonal where length equals width.
animations: Display set of all rectangles on the curve in #ADFF2F.
Animate rectangle morphing continuously into a square.
Highlight diagonal constraint where side lengths match in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Application & Conclusion
lecture_lines: The Square Peg Problem remains fascinating.
Topology proves existence even without coordinates.
A perfect fit is mathematically guaranteed.
animations: Display parking a square vehicle against a curved wall in #00CED1.
Visualize the point where all four vertices touch in #FF1493.
